headline: NATO jets scrambled over Poland as Russia hits western Ukraine
dek: After Russian strikes (UAVs) on western Ukraine near the Polish border, Polish + allied military aviation operated in Polish airspace 'preventively'; Lublin and Rzeszów airports suspended civilian flights; ground-based air defense and radar reconnaissance placed on readiness.
sources: Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces (RSZ) — X statement; Polish Air Navigation Services Agency — X statement
fault_line: Is NATO's eastern flank genuinely at risk of spillover, or is repeated scrambling theater that normalizes confrontation?

sections.what_happened: After Russian strikes (UAVs) on western Ukraine near the Polish border, Polish + allied military aviation operated in Polish airspace 'preventively'; Lublin and Rzeszów airports suspended civilian flights; ground-based air defense and radar reconnaissance placed on readiness.
sections.what_verified: Multiple outlets carry the Polish Armed Forces statement verbatim; RCB alert for Lublin/Subcarpathian regions later canceled (Ukrinform). Romania also scrambled F-16s Oct 17 over Black Sea drone activity (Romanian MoD).
sections.what_disputed: None — measures described by Poland itself as preventive; no airspace violation reported. Framing as 'NATO intercepting' would be false.
sections.why_matters: Third preventive scramble in three days — jets in the air in Warsaw while Trump pulls sanctions off the table in Washington. The split: NATO's posture hardens as US diplomacy eases. Fault line: is the eastern flank at real risk, or is this pressure theater?
sections.context: Background: NATO jets scrambled over Poland as Russia hits western Ukraine — Lublin & Rzeszów airports closed (Oct 19)

totw_analysis: Our read: Third preventive scramble in three days — jets in the air in Warsaw while Trump pulls sanctions off the table in Washington. The split: NATO's posture hardens as US diplomacy eases. Fault line: is the eastern flank at real risk, or is this pressure theater? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is NATO's eastern flank genuinely at risk of spillover, or is repeated scrambling theater that normalizes confrontation?
